summary: Columbus City Schools supports the Commission's goals but urges the Commission to preserve E-Rate support for essential infrastructure services and avoid imposing uniform screen-time limits. The District emphasizes the importance of maintaining clear distinctions between district-managed networks, district-owned devices, and personally owned devices. Columbus City Schools recommends that the Commission evaluate continuing E-Rate need based on affordability, capacity, reliability, infrastructure  The text discusses the need for E-Rate support in school districts, including the Columbus City Schools example. It highlights the importance of connectivity for educational purposes but emphasizes that connectivity alone does not guarantee affordability or sustainability. The text also addresses the need for sufficient implementation time and guidance before enforcing new requirements. The text opposes limiting or sunsetting E-Rate, arguing that it would reduce funding for broadband access and  The comment emphasizes the importance of maintaining a broad interpretation of educational purposes to ensure that E-Rate-funded networks are used primarily for educational purposes. It argues that reducing the definition to a narrow stand-alone measure of screen time would hinder the effectivenes

claims.argument: The final rule should not force applicants to choose between FCC timing rules and applicable state or local law.
claims.evidence_quote:
The Commission should clarify how any new requirement applies to: 
• 
Multi-year contracts 
• 
Voluntary extensions 
• 
State master contracts 
• 
Cooperative agreements 
• 
Month-to-month services 
• 
Tariffed or regulated services 
• 
Existing contracts that remain legally valid 
• 
Contracts amended to reﬂect changing service needs
